97	# /architecture-review — Phase 1: Load Everything
98	
99	> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
100	> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.
101	
102	## Phase 1: Load Everything
103	
104	**In this file:**
105	
106	- Phase 1a — L0: Summary Scan (fast, low tokens)
107	- Phase 1b — L1/L2: Targeted Section Load
108	- Design Documents
109	- Architecture Documents
110	- Engine Reference
111	- Project Standards
112	
113	### Phase 1a — L0: Summary Scan (fast, low tokens)
114	
115	**Freshness check before any scan.** Locate the latest prior report — Glob
116	`docs/architecture/architecture-review-*.md` and take the newest — then:
117	
118	```
119	Bash: bash .claude/scripts/review-receipts.sh check "[latest-report]" docs/architecture/adr-*.md design/gdd/*.md
120	```
121	
122	- **Any `UNRESOLVED`** — check this FIRST; it disqualifies every option
123	  below. One of the two globs matched no file, so that whole document class
124	  was never examined and the comparison covered less than it appears to.
125	  Say which pattern came back unresolved and stop: an ADR or GDD directory
126	  that is empty, renamed or misspelled is a finding about the project, not a
127	  reason to stand on a prior report. Never read a set of `UNCHANGED` lines as
128	  "everything is current" while an `UNRESOLVED` line is present — the set
129	  compared was not the set requested.
130	- **Everything `UNCHANGED`** (and no `UNRESOLVED`) — nothing this review
131	  reads has changed since that report; re-running reproduces it. Surface the
132	  prior report's date and verdict and offer via `AskUserQuestion`: `[A] Stand
133	  on the prior report (Recommended)` / `[B] Re-run the full review anyway` —
134	  `guided` proceeds with [A] and notes it; `autonomous` logs via
135	  `log_decision` and stands on the prior report.
136	- **Some `CHANGED`/`NEW`** — name them, then scope instead of re-running
137	  everything: recommend `/architecture-review [system]` (single-system mode)
138	  for just the changed systems. A full re-run stays available on request,
139	  and structural changes (a `NEW` ADR, a deleted file) warrant one.
140	- **`RECEIPT: NONE`** — no prior report, or one written before receipts
141	  existed. Proceed with the full review; this run's report will carry the
142	  first stamps.
143	
144	Before reading any full document, use Grep to extract `## Summary` sections
145	from all GDDs and ADRs:
146	
147	```
148	Grep pattern="## Summary" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -A 4
149	Grep pattern="## Summary" glob="docs/architecture/adr-*.md" output_mode="content" -A 3
150	```
151	
152	**Fail open on a missing Summary.** Establish the denominator: glob
153	`design/gdd/*.md` and count **N**. A scan matching fewer than N means those GDDs
154	predate `## Summary` (`/design-system` emits it, but older GDDs lack it) — never
155	treat an absent Summary as a system out of scope. A zero-match scan means "no GDD
156	carries a Summary yet", not "nothing to review": full-read the unmatched set.
157	
158	For `single-gdd [path]` mode: use the target GDD's summary to identify which
159	ADRs reference the same system (Grep ADRs for the system name), then load only
160	those ADRs' sections per Phase 1b. Skip unrelated GDDs entirely.
161	
162	For `engine` mode: load ADR sections only — GDDs are not needed for engine checks.
163	In practice this is the `## Engine Compatibility` scan alone.
164	
165	For `coverage` or `full` mode: proceed to Phase 1b for the full in-scope set.
166	**This is a section load, not a full-file load** — see below for why, and for the
167	narrow cases that still justify escalating to a whole document.
168	
169	### Phase 1b — L1/L2: Targeted Section Load
170	
171	Load the sections the later phases actually consume — **not whole files**. This
172	skill reads the two largest document sets in the project (every GDD *and* every
173	ADR); at realistic sizes a full load of both exhausts the context window before
174	Phase 2 starts, and most of what it loads is narrative this skill never uses.
175	
176	**Establish the denominator first.** Glob `design/gdd/*.md` and count **N_gdd**;
177	glob `docs/architecture/adr-*.md` and count **N_adr**. Report both. A section
178	scan matching fewer than the denominator means those documents lack the section —
179	**never treat an absent section as an absent document.** The scan narrows the
180	*read* set; it never shrinks the *in-scope* set.
181	
182	### Design Documents
183	
184	Phase 2 extracts *technical requirements* — data structures, performance
185	constraints, engine capabilities, cross-system communication, persistence,
186	threading, platform needs. Those live in a known set of sections; Overview and
187	Player Fantasy are narrative and yield none.
188	
189	```
190	Grep pattern="^## (Detailed Rules|Detailed Design|Formulas|Dependencies|Tuning Knobs|Acceptance Criteria)" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -A 40
191	```
192	
193	Accept **either** `## Detailed Rules` or `## Detailed Design` — the design
194	standard and the GDD template disagree on the name and they denote the same
195	required section. Full-read a single GDD only when a scanned section
196	cross-references material outside itself, or when a GDD matched zero sections
197	(it predates the template — read it whole and say so).
198	
199	- `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — the authoritative list of systems; read whole (small, and it is an index)
200	
201	### Architecture Documents
202	
203	Phases 3–5 need the traceability table, the decision itself, engine claims, and
204	the dependency edges — not Context, Consequences, Alternatives, Migration Plan or
205	Validation Criteria, which explain *why* a decision was made.
206	
207	```
208	Grep pattern="^## (Status|Decision|GDD Requirements Addressed|Engine Compatibility|ADR Dependencies|Performance Implications)" glob="docs/architecture/adr-*.md" output_mode="content" -A 30
209	```
210	
211	Interpret against **N_adr**, and distinguish the two zero-match cases — they are
212	not the same finding:
213	
214	| Result | Meaning | Action |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| N_adr matches | Normal. | Proceed on the scanned sections. |
217	| Some ADRs match, some do not | Those ADRs are missing sections. | Record each as a **structural gap** in the Phase 7 report — a missing `## GDD Requirements Addressed` is itself a traceability finding. |
218	| **0 matches, N_adr > 0** | **Malformed ADRs**, not "no architecture". | "[N_adr] ADRs found, none carries a scannable section — run `/architecture-decision retrofit [file]` on each." Do **not** report zero coverage; that would read as a design failure when it is a format failure. |
219	
220	Escalate to a full read of one ADR only when judging a conflict needs its
221	reasoning (Phase 4) — that is a per-ADR decision, not a blanket load.
222	
223	- `docs/architecture/architecture.md` if it exists
224	
225	### Engine Reference
226	- `docs/engine-reference/[engine]/VERSION.md`
227	- `docs/engine-reference/[engine]/breaking-changes.md`
228	- `docs/engine-reference/[engine]/deprecated-apis.md`
229	- **Only the module docs the in-scope ADRs actually name** — take the union of
230	  each ADR's `References Consulted` and `Post-Cutoff APIs Used` fields (already
231	  captured by the `## Engine Compatibility` scan above) and read those files.
232	  Reading the whole `modules/` directory loads engine subsystems the project may
233	  not use at all. If no ADR names any module, read none and note it: Phase 5
234	  cannot cross-check engine claims that were never made.
235	
236	### Project Standards
237	- `project.yaml` — `naming.*` and `performance.*`; plus `.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` for those keys when absent and for forbidden patterns / allowed libraries
238	
239	Report a count: "Loaded [N] GDDs, [M] ADRs, engine: [name + version]."
240	
241	**Also read `docs/consistency-failures.md`** if it exists. Extract entries with
242	Domain matching the systems under review (Architecture, Engine, or any GDD domain
243	being covered). Surface recurring patterns as a "Known conflict-prone areas" note
244	at the top of the Phase 4 conflict detection output.
245	
246	---

# /architecture-review — Phase 1: Load Everything

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 1: Load Everything

**In this file:**

- Phase 1a — L0: Summary Scan (fast, low tokens)
- Phase 1b — L1/L2: Targeted Section Load
- Design Documents
- Architecture Documents
- Engine Reference
- Project Standards

### Phase 1a — L0: Summary Scan (fast, low tokens)

**Freshness check before any scan.** Locate the latest prior report — Glob
`docs/architecture/architecture-review-*.md` and take the newest — then:

```
Bash: bash .claude/scripts/review-receipts.sh check "[latest-report]" docs/architecture/adr-*.md design/gdd/*.md
```

- **Any `UNRESOLVED`** — check this FIRST; it disqualifies every option
  below. One of the two globs matched no file, so that whole document class
  was never examined and the comparison covered less than it appears to.
  Say which pattern came back unresolved and stop: an ADR or GDD directory
  that is empty, renamed or misspelled is a finding about the project, not a
  reason to stand on a prior report. Never read a set of `UNCHANGED` lines as
  "everything is current" while an `UNRESOLVED` line is present — the set
  compared was not the set requested.
- **Everything `UNCHANGED`** (and no `UNRESOLVED`) — nothing this review
  reads has changed since that report; re-running reproduces it. Surface the
  prior report's date and verdict and offer via `AskUserQuestion`: `[A] Stand
  on the prior report (Recommended)` / `[B] Re-run the full review anyway` —
  `guided` proceeds with [A] and notes it; `autonomous` logs via
  `log_decision` and stands on the prior report.
- **Some `CHANGED`/`NEW`** — name them, then scope instead of re-running
  everything: recommend `/architecture-review [system]` (single-system mode)
  for just the changed systems. A full re-run stays available on request,
  and structural changes (a `NEW` ADR, a deleted file) warrant one.
- **`RECEIPT: NONE`** — no prior report, or one written before receipts
  existed. Proceed with the full review; this run's report will carry the
  first stamps.

Before reading any full document, use Grep to extract `## Summary` sections
from all GDDs and ADRs:

```
Grep pattern="## Summary" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -A 4
Grep pattern="## Summary" glob="docs/architecture/adr-*.md" output_mode="content" -A 3
```

**Fail open on a missing Summary.** Establish the denominator: glob
`design/gdd/*.md` and count **N**. A scan matching fewer than N means those GDDs
predate `## Summary` (`/design-system` emits it, but older GDDs lack it) — never
treat an absent Summary as a system out of scope. A zero-match scan means "no GDD
carries a Summary yet", not "nothing to review": full-read the unmatched set.

For `single-gdd [path]` mode: use the target GDD's summary to identify which
ADRs reference the same system (Grep ADRs for the system name), then load only
those ADRs' sections per Phase 1b. Skip unrelated GDDs entirely.

For `engine` mode: load ADR sections only — GDDs are not needed for engine checks.
In practice this is the `## Engine Compatibility` scan alone.

For `coverage` or `full` mode: proceed to Phase 1b for the full in-scope set.
**This is a section load, not a full-file load** — see below for why, and for the
narrow cases that still justify escalating to a whole document.

### Phase 1b — L1/L2: Targeted Section Load

Load the sections the later phases actually consume — **not whole files**. This
skill reads the two largest document sets in the project (every GDD *and* every
ADR); at realistic sizes a full load of both exhausts the context window before
Phase 2 starts, and most of what it loads is narrative this skill never uses.

**Establish the denominator first.** Glob `design/gdd/*.md` and count **N_gdd**;
glob `docs/architecture/adr-*.md` and count **N_adr**. Report both. A section
scan matching fewer than the denominator means those documents lack the section —
**never treat an absent section as an absent document.** The scan narrows the
*read* set; it never shrinks the *in-scope* set.

### Design Documents

Phase 2 extracts *technical requirements* — data structures, performance
constraints, engine capabilities, cross-system communication, persistence,
threading, platform needs. Those live in a known set of sections; Overview and
Player Fantasy are narrative and yield none.

```
Grep pattern="^## (Detailed Rules|Detailed Design|Formulas|Dependencies|Tuning Knobs|Acceptance Criteria)" glob="design/gdd/*.md" output_mode="content" -A 40
```

Accept **either** `## Detailed Rules` or `## Detailed Design` — the design
standard and the GDD template disagree on the name and they denote the same
required section. Full-read a single GDD only when a scanned section
cross-references material outside itself, or when a GDD matched zero sections
(it predates the template — read it whole and say so).

- `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — the authoritative list of systems; read whole (small, and it is an index)

### Architecture Documents

Phases 3–5 need the traceability table, the decision itself, engine claims, and
the dependency edges — not Context, Consequences, Alternatives, Migration Plan or
Validation Criteria, which explain *why* a decision was made.

```
Grep pattern="^## (Status|Decision|GDD Requirements Addressed|Engine Compatibility|ADR Dependencies|Performance Implications)" glob="docs/architecture/adr-*.md" output_mode="content" -A 30
```

Interpret against **N_adr**, and distinguish the two zero-match cases — they are
not the same finding:

| Result | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| N_adr matches | Normal. | Proceed on the scanned sections. |
| Some ADRs match, some do not | Those ADRs are missing sections. | Record each as a **structural gap** in the Phase 7 report — a missing `## GDD Requirements Addressed` is itself a traceability finding. |
| **0 matches, N_adr > 0** | **Malformed ADRs**, not "no architecture". | "[N_adr] ADRs found, none carries a scannable section — run `/architecture-decision retrofit [file]` on each." Do **not** report zero coverage; that would read as a design failure when it is a format failure. |

Escalate to a full read of one ADR only when judging a conflict needs its
reasoning (Phase 4) — that is a per-ADR decision, not a blanket load.

- `docs/architecture/architecture.md` if it exists

### Engine Reference
- `docs/engine-reference/[engine]/VERSION.md`
- `docs/engine-reference/[engine]/breaking-changes.md`
- `docs/engine-reference/[engine]/deprecated-apis.md`
- **Only the module docs the in-scope ADRs actually name** — take the union of
  each ADR's `References Consulted` and `Post-Cutoff APIs Used` fields (already
  captured by the `## Engine Compatibility` scan above) and read those files.
  Reading the whole `modules/` directory loads engine subsystems the project may
  not use at all. If no ADR names any module, read none and note it: Phase 5
  cannot cross-check engine claims that were never made.

### Project Standards
- `project.yaml` — `naming.*` and `performance.*`; plus `.claude/docs/technical-preferences.md` for those keys when absent and for forbidden patterns / allowed libraries

Report a count: "Loaded [N] GDDs, [M] ADRs, engine: [name + version]."

**Also read `docs/consistency-failures.md`** if it exists. Extract entries with
Domain matching the systems under review (Architecture, Engine, or any GDD domain
being covered). Surface recurring patterns as a "Known conflict-prone areas" note
at the top of the Phase 4 conflict detection output.

# /architecture-review — Phase 2: Extract Technical Requirements

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 2: Extract Technical Requirements from Every GDD

### Pre-load the TR Registry

Before extracting any requirements, read `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
if it exists. Index existing entries by `id` and by normalized `requirement`
text (lowercase, trimmed). This prevents ID renumbering across review runs.

For each requirement you extract, the matching rule is:
1. **Exact/near match** to an existing registry entry for the same system →
   reuse that entry's TR-ID unchanged. Update the `requirement` text in the
   registry only if the GDD wording changed (same intent, clearer phrasing) —
   add a `revised: [date]` field.
2. **No match** → assign a new ID: next available `TR-[system]-NNN` for that
   system, starting from the highest existing sequence + 1.
3. **Ambiguous** (partial match, intent unclear) → ask the user:
   > "Does '[new requirement text]' refer to the same requirement as
   > `TR-[system]-NNN: [existing text]'`, or is it a new requirement?"
   User answers: "Same requirement" (reuse ID) or "New requirement" (new ID).

For any requirement with `status: deprecated` in the registry — skip it.
It was removed from the GDD intentionally.

For each GDD, read it and extract all **technical requirements** — things the
architecture must provide for the system to work. A technical requirement is any
statement that implies a specific architectural decision.

Categories to extract:

| Category | Example |
|----------|---------|
| **Data structures** | "Each entity has health, max health, status effects" → needs a component/data schema |
| **Performance constraints** | "Collision detection must run at 60fps with 200 entities" → physics budget ADR |
| **Engine capability** | "Inverse kinematics for character animation" → IK system ADR |
| **Cross-system communication** | "Damage system notifies UI and audio simultaneously" → event/signal architecture ADR |
| **State persistence** | "Player progress persists between sessions" → save system ADR |
| **Threading/timing** | "AI decisions happen off the main thread" → concurrency ADR |
| **Platform requirements** | "Supports keyboard, gamepad, touch" → input system ADR |

For each GDD, produce a structured list:

```
GDD: [filename]
System: [system name]
Technical Requirements:
  TR-[GDD]-001: [requirement text] → Domain: [Physics/Rendering/etc]
  TR-[GDD]-002: [requirement text] → Domain: [...]
```

This becomes the **requirements baseline** — the complete set of what the
architecture must cover.

# /architecture-review — Phases 3 and 3b: Traceability Matrix and Story Linkage

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 3: Build the Traceability Matrix

**In this file:**

- Step 3b-1 — Load stories
- Step 3b-2 — Load test files
- Step 3b-3 — Build the extended RTM

For each technical requirement extracted in Phase 2, search the ADRs:

1. Use the ADRs **already loaded in Phase 1b** — do not re-read them. Extract each
   ADR's "GDD Requirements Addressed" section from what is already in context.
   (If Phase 1b ran in a mode that did not load every ADR, `Grep pattern="## GDD
   Requirements Addressed" glob="docs/architecture/adr-*.md" output_mode="content"
   -A 15` fills the gap without a full re-read.)
2. Check if it explicitly references the requirement or its GDD
3. Check if the ADR's decision text implicitly covers the requirement
4. Mark coverage status:

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| ✅ **Covered** | An **Accepted** ADR explicitly addresses this requirement |
| 🟡 **Covered (Proposed)** | An ADR addresses it, but that ADR is still `Proposed` |
| ⚠️ **Partial** | An ADR partially covers this, or coverage is ambiguous |
| ❌ **Gap** | No ADR addresses this requirement |
| ❓ **Not assessed** | The ADR is unreadable, or has no `## Status` section |

> **Read each ADR's `## Status` before marking coverage — an unaccepted decision
> is not coverage.** If `✅` meant only that *an ADR addresses this*, with no
> status qualification, a requirement covered entirely by `Proposed` ADRs would
> count as covered and this review could return **PASS: All requirements
> covered** over an architecture nobody had accepted. Four skills downstream
> (`create-control-manifest`, `create-epics`, `create-stories`, `gate-check`)
> require `Accepted`, so a PASS on that basis sends work forward that every one
> of them will refuse.
>
> `🟡` is **not** a pass state: it caps the verdict at **CONCERNS**, and names the
> route out — `/architecture-decision accept ADR-NNNN`. That route is the only
> thing that moves an ADR to `Accepted`; without it, grading `Proposed` as
> covered would be the only option, which is why it must never be graded so.

Build the full matrix:

```
## Traceability Matrix

| Requirement ID | GDD | System | Requirement | ADR Coverage | Status |
|---------------|-----|--------|-------------|--------------|--------|
| TR-combat-001 | combat.md | Combat | Hitbox detection < 1 frame | ADR-0003 | ✅ |
| TR-combat-002 | combat.md | Combat | Combo window timing | — | ❌ GAP |
| TR-inventory-001 | inventory.md | Inventory | Persistent item storage | ADR-0005 | ✅ |
```

Count the totals: X covered, Y partial, Z gaps.

---

## Phase 3b: Story and Test Linkage (RTM mode only)

*Skip this phase unless the argument is `rtm` or `full` with stories present.*

This phase extends the Phase 3 matrix to include the story that implements
each requirement and the test that verifies it — producing the full
Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM).

### Step 3b-1 — Load stories

Glob `production/epics/**/*.md` (excluding EPIC.md index files) to establish the
denominator. Then collect the fields with **targeted section greps, not a full
read of each story** — the same two-grep form `/test-evidence-review` uses for
this identical extraction:

```
Grep pattern="## Test Evidence" glob="production/epics/**/story-*.md" output_mode="content" -A 8
Grep pattern="TR-" glob="production/epics/**/story-*.md" output_mode="content"
```

- **TR-ID** — from the second grep.
- **Test file path** — under `## Test Evidence`, captured by the first grep's `-A 8`.
- **Status** — from the story header; add `Grep pattern="^> \*\*Status\*\*"` if not already captured.
- **Story path and title** — from the file name and path; no read at all.

Full-read a story only when its Test Evidence section is missing or ambiguous.

### Step 3b-2 — Load test files

Glob the engine's test root (`.claude/docs/directory-structure.md`): Godot
`tests/unit/**/*_test.*` and `tests/integration/**/*_test.*`; Unity
`Assets/Tests/**/*Tests.cs`; Unreal `Source/*/Private/Tests/**/*.cpp`. With no
engine configured, say the test index could not be built rather than reading an
empty glob as "no tests". Build an index: system → [test file paths].

For each test file path from Step 3b-1, confirm via Glob whether the file
actually exists. Note MISSING if the stated path does not exist.

### Step 3b-3 — Build the extended RTM

For each TR-ID in the Phase 3 matrix, add:
- **Story**: the story file path(s) that reference this TR-ID (may be multiple)
- **Test File**: the test file path stated in the story's Test Evidence section
- **Test Status**: COVERED (test file exists) / MISSING (path stated but not
  found) / NONE (no test path stated, story type may be Visual/Feel/UI) /
  NO STORY (requirement has no story yet — pre-production gap)

Extended matrix format:

```
## Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)

| TR-ID | GDD | Requirement | ADR | Story | Test File | Test Status |
|-------|-----|-------------|-----|-------|-----------|-------------|
| TR-combat-001 | combat.md | Hitbox < 1 frame | ADR-0003 | story-001-hitbox.md | tests/unit/combat/hitbox_test.gd | COVERED |
| TR-combat-002 | combat.md | Combo window | — | story-002-combo.md | — | NONE (Visual/Feel) |
| TR-inventory-001 | inventory.md | Persistent storage | ADR-0005 | — | — | NO STORY |
```

RTM coverage summary:
- COVERED: [N] — requirements with ADR + story + passing test
- MISSING test: [N] — story exists but test file not found
- NO STORY: [N] — requirements with ADR but no story yet
- NO ADR: [N] — requirements without architectural coverage (from Phase 3 gaps)
- Full chain complete (COVERED): [N/total] ([%])

# /architecture-review — Phase 4: Cross-ADR Conflict Detection

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 4: Cross-ADR Conflict Detection

Compare every ADR against every other ADR to detect contradictions. A conflict
exists when:

- **Data ownership conflict**: Two ADRs claim exclusive ownership of the same data
- **Integration contract conflict**: ADR-A assumes System X has interface Y, but
  ADR-B defines System X with a different interface
- **Performance budget conflict**: ADR-A allocates N ms to physics, ADR-B allocates
  N ms to AI, together they exceed the total frame budget
- **Dependency cycle**: ADR-A says System X initialises before Y; ADR-B says Y
  initialises before X
- **Architecture pattern conflict**: ADR-A uses event-driven communication for a
  subsystem; ADR-B uses direct function calls to the same subsystem
- **State management conflict**: Two ADRs define authority over the same game state
  (e.g. both Combat ADR and Character ADR claim to own the health value)

For each conflict found:

```
## Conflict: [ADR-NNNN] vs [ADR-MMMM]
Type: [Data ownership / Integration / Performance / Dependency / Pattern / State]
ADR-NNNN claims: [...]
ADR-MMMM claims: [...]
Impact: [What breaks if both are implemented as written]
Resolution options:
  1. [Option A]
  2. [Option B]
```

### ADR Dependency Ordering

After conflict detection, analyse the dependency graph across all ADRs.

**Build the graph deterministically — do not trace it by hand:**

```
Bash: bash .claude/scripts/adr-dep-graph.sh
```

It collects every `Depends On` edge, runs Kahn's algorithm, and emits
`ADRS:` / `EDGES:` / `NO_DEPS_SECTION:` / `CYCLE:`. A model tracing A→B→C→A across
a dozen ADRs eventually misses an edge; the algorithm cannot. It reports
observations, not a verdict — you apply the meaning below.

**`NO_DEPS_SECTION` is load-bearing**: it makes "no cycles because the graph is
clean" distinguishable from "no cycles because half the ADRs declare no
dependencies". Report the second case as a structural gap, never as a clean graph.

Then interpret:

1. **Topological sort**: the emitted order — ADRs with no
   dependencies come first (Foundation), ADRs that depend on those come next, etc.
2. **Flag unresolved dependencies**: cross the `EDGES:` list against the `## Status`
   values already scanned in Phase 1b. If ADR-A depends on an ADR that is still
   `Proposed` or does not exist, flag it:
   ```
   ⚠️  ADR-0005 depends on ADR-0002 — but ADR-0002 is still Proposed.
       ADR-0005 cannot be safely implemented until ADR-0002 is Accepted.
   ```
3. **Cycle detection**: every `CYCLE:` line the script emitted is a
   `DEPENDENCY CYCLE` — report each one. Do not re-derive them by hand:
   ```
   🔴 DEPENDENCY CYCLE: ADR-0003 → ADR-0006 → ADR-0003
      This cycle must be broken before either can be implemented.
   ```
4. **Output recommended implementation order**:
   ```
   ### Recommended ADR Implementation Order (topologically sorted)
   Foundation (no dependencies):
     1. ADR-0001: [title]
     2. ADR-0003: [title]
   Depends on Foundation:
     3. ADR-0002: [title] (requires ADR-0001)
     4. ADR-0005: [title] (requires ADR-0003)
   Feature layer:
     5. ADR-0004: [title] (requires ADR-0002, ADR-0005)
   ```

# /architecture-review — Phases 5 and 5b: Engine Cross-Check and Design Revision Flags

> Part of `/architecture-review`. `SKILL.md` names when to read this file; the settings it
> resolved and the rules under its later headings still apply here.

## Phase 5: Engine Compatibility Cross-Check

**In this file:**

- Version Consistency
- Post-Cutoff API Consistency
- Deprecated API Check
- Missing Engine Compatibility Sections
- Engine Specialist Consultation

Across all ADRs, check for engine consistency:

### Version Consistency
- Do all ADRs that mention an engine version agree on the same version?
- If any ADR was written for an older engine version, flag it as potentially stale

### Post-Cutoff API Consistency
- Collect all "Post-Cutoff APIs Used" fields from all ADRs
- For each, verify against the relevant module reference doc
- Check that no two ADRs make contradictory assumptions about the same post-cutoff API

### Deprecated API Check
- Grep all ADRs for API names listed in `deprecated-apis.md`
- Flag any ADR referencing a deprecated API

### Missing Engine Compatibility Sections
- List all ADRs that are missing the Engine Compatibility section entirely

All ten documents consistently target Engine Compatibility 4.7.2, and my grep for deprecated usage only turns up mentions within ban lists, not actual deprecated calls. The `duplicate()` references in ADR-0003 and ADR-0005 likely point to `duplicate_deep`, which I'll leave for the specialist to confirm, and I'm now checking ADR-0003 for post-cutoff conflicts.

I'm noting the module docs (input, physics, networking, rendering) for the specialist to review, then planning the parallel agent spawn: ten coverage agents writing candidate files per ADR, a Phase 4 conflict agent to verify residuals and scan high-risk ownership/interface areas while I run the dependency graph script myself, a godot-specialist for Phase 5, and a Phase 6 agent to compare architecture.md against something I'm still defining.

That rounds out to thirteen agents total — manageable. I'll write the candidate files first, letting agents grep ADR headings themselves rather than pre-extracting line ranges, and instruct them to write full results to a session-specific scratchpad file while returning only short summaries, since that's safer for durability than risking huge direct returns.

content.thinking:
I'm tracing a dependency cycle involving ADR-0010, 0007, 0005, and 0004, noting that 0010 gets pulled in as a soft dependency through 0004's and 0005's "Depends On" cells, which loops back through 0007's validation-only link to 0005.

On closer inspection, the cycle only exists through soft edges, which TD-27 never intended to be circular — the script just can't tell hard deps from soft ones. If I strip the soft edges (0004→0010, 0005→0010, 0007→0005), the acceptance graph is actually acyclic: 0010 only truly requires 0007 Accepted, and 0007's real requirements are 0001, 0003, and a spike, not 0005. I'll treat this as a structural documentation issue — move the soft-dependency mentions out of the Depends On cells into a Related/Ordering Note — flagged as CONCERNS rather than a blocking design conflict, then move on to spawning the coverage agents.

I found 4 dependency cycles, all routed through the "soft" edges flagged in the ADRs (0004→0010, 0005→0010, 0007→0005), which I'll note in the report. Now launching 10 coverage agents (one per ADR) plus a cross-ADR conflict agent, a Godot specialist, and an architecture-doc agent, all running on Sonnet.

"""Regenerate docs/architecture/requirements-traceability.md from base.json + final.json + registry."""
import json, re, sys, collections
S = sys.argv[1]
OUT = 'docs/architecture/requirements-traceability.md'
b = json.load(open(S + '/base.json'))
fin = json.load(open(S + '/final.json'))
reg_txt = open('docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml', encoding='utf-8').read()
reg = {}
for e in re.split(r'\n(?=- id: )', reg_txt):
    m = re.match(r'- id: (TR-[a-z]+-\d{3})', e)
    if m:
        r = re.search(r'\n  requirement: "(.*)"\n', e)
        rv = re.search(r'\n  revised: "?([^"\n]*)"?', e)
        reg[m.group(1)] = dict(req=r.group(1).replace('\\"', '"') if r else '', revised=rv.group(1) if rv else '')

RETAG = {  # ADR-0007 "owned elsewhere" table: rule owner, not the pipeline
    'TR-itemdb-015': 'GDD-owned (Item DB IDB-17)', 'TR-boarding-019': 'GDD-owned (Boarding)',

Last Updated: 2026-10-28 (second review, after Foundation ADR-0004..0010)

- Total requirements: {total}
- Covered (Accepted ADR): 0 (0.0%). No ADR is Accepted yet; all ten are Proposed.
- Covered (Proposed ADR): {stat['cov']} ({100*stat['cov']/total:.1f}%)
- Partial: {stat['part']} ({100*stat['part']/total:.1f}%)
- Gaps: {stat['gap']} ({100*stat['gap']/total:.1f}%)

| Layer of planned ADR | Covered (Proposed) | Partial | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|

Method: each of the 10 written ADRs was graded (COVERED / PARTIAL / NOT) against every requirement that is planned for it or that it cites (461 + new rows), by one reviewer per ADR. Requirements planned only for ADR-0011..0034 were not graded against the written ADRs; they are Gap because their planned ADR is unwritten. A requirement takes its best grade across ADRs.

Status key: 🟡 Covered (Proposed): a Proposed ADR addresses every clause (not a pass state until Accepted). ⚠️ Partial: an ADR addresses some clauses or defers a clause elsewhere. ❌ Gap: no written ADR addresses it. ⛔ in Note: the ADR decides something the requirement text contradicts (see the review's GDD Revision Flags). `GDD-owned` in Planned ADR: ADR-0007 loads and checks the data but the rule is a GDD rule (ADR-0007 owned-elsewhere table).
"""

body = out[start:]
gaps = ['', '## Known Gaps', '', 'Grouped by planned ADR (most foundational first). Write the ADR with `/architecture-decision`; for a written ADR, the gap is a clause it does not decide.', '',
        '| Planned ADR | Gaps | Requirement IDs |', '|---|---|---|']

    n = re.findall(r'ADR-(\d{4})', p); return (int(n[0]) if n else 999, p)

parts = ['', '## Partial Coverage', '', '| Requirement ID | Planned ADR | ADR Coverage | What is missing |', '|---|---|---|---|']

for t, cf in conflicts: sup.append(f'| {t} | {cell(" / ".join(cf))} |')

## Specialist findings

### E1 [HIGH] `PresentationViews.get()` overrides native `Object.get()` and will not load
- **Where:** ADR-0003 l.340 (`func get(block_id: StringName) -> Object` in `class_name PresentationViews extends RefCounted`). Also used at ADR-0009 l.570 ("its `PresentationViews.get` returns `empty_view`"). ADR-0009 l.119 and ADR-0010 OQ-K (l.685) depend on this class.
- **Claim:** the facet exposes `get(block_id)`.
- **Reality:** probed on 4.7.2 (P-A). `func get(block_id: StringName) -> Object` in a `RefCounted` script gives `Parse Error: The method "get()" overrides a method from native class "Object". This won't be called by the engine and may not work as expected. (Warning treated as error.)` The script then fails to load (`Failed to load script ... Parse error`). `NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE` is an error by default, per the output of this run (the probe project set no warning options).
- **Contradiction inside the set:** ADR-0010 l.146 forbids accessors named `get`, `set`, `free`, `call` and the rest ("`NATIVE_METHOD_OVERRIDE`"), yet ADR-0003 and ADR-0009 define one.
- **Confidence:** HIGH, probed.
- **GDD:** no GDD names `PresentationViews.get`. My grep of `design/gdd/*.md` for `PresentationViews|views\.get\(|\.get\(&"` found no hits outside the ADRs. Fix: rename to `get_view` or `lookup`, and update ADR-0003 §7, ADR-0009 l.119/570 and ADR-0010 l.146.

### E2 [MEDIUM] Time-scale risk text is stale: `time_scale` is now probed
- **Where:** ADR-0001 l.27 item (2), l.51, l.238 ("`Engine.time_scale` scales `delta` differently in 4.7.2" is listed as a risk and a spike item).
- **Reality (P-C, headless):** over 1.0 s of real time the sum of `_process` delta was 1.006 at scale 1.0, 0.502 at 0.5, and 2.010 at 2.0. So `_process(delta)` IS scaled by `Engine.time_scale`. The ADR's mitigation (pin 1.0 in release, flag `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT`) is correct and sufficient. Item (2) can be marked probed for headless. A release export and the windowed editor remain unchecked.
- **Confidence:** HIGH on headless, probed.
- **GDD:** `design/gdd/debug-overlay-true-values.md:499` says the sanity-drift fold is independent of `Engine.time_scale`. That holds only if the fold is driven by ticks T, not by `delta`, and this is consistent with a tick-driven kernel. Nothing contradicted.

### E3 [LOW] ADR-0006 rename-over-existing on Windows
- **Where:** ADR-0006 l.27 probe (1).
- **Claim:** the author's recollection (65%, UNVERIFIED) is that `DirAccessWindows::rename` is remove-then-rename, not an atomic `MoveFileEx`. The ADR therefore never claims atomicity.
- **Reality:** my own recollection of the engine source agrees (it removes an existing target first), MED confidence, not probed. The ADR's conservative design (generations plus verify) already covers this. No change needed. Keep it on the UNVERIFIED list until a kill-between-remove-and-rename test exists.

### E4 [MEDIUM] "by value" wording contradicts packed-array reference semantics
- **Where:** ADR-0010 IO-02 (l.309), l.391 and l.878 ("handed over by value and never mutated afterwards") versus ADR-0006 §1.6 and probes 16 and 7 (packed arrays alias by reference; ownership transfer or `.duplicate()` is required).
- **Reality:** the engine does not copy on pass to `Thread.start(callable.bind(...))` or on assignment. "By value" misleads a lint author or implementer. The rule should read "ownership transferred (no retained alias) or `.duplicate()`d".
- **Confidence:** HIGH (ADR-0006 probe 16 and ADR-0005 P7). Not re-probed by me.
- **GDD:** none found. I did not grep GDDs for this.

### E5 [MEDIUM] SIM-09 versus the ADR-0002 untyped payload boundary: reconciled only by an empty allow-list
- **Where:** ADR-0010 l.292 (SIM-09) and OQ-H l.682, versus ADR-0002 l.26.
- **Claim:** untyped `Dictionary` is required at the command payload boundary. SIM-09 bans a bare `Dictionary` in the sim layers except allow-listed files.
- **Reality:** no engine conflict. The risk is process: the allow-list `dictionary_variant.json` is not yet written (OQ-H), so a lint pass would fail every payload validator. Also, per ADR-0010 l.230, `Dictionary[K,V].keys()` and `.values()` return untyped `Array` (4.4), which interacts with the same SIM-09 bare-`Array` ban.
- **Confidence:** HIGH on reading, not probed.

### E6 [LOW] Engine reference is wrong about the Windows default renderer driver
- **Where:** VERSION.md timeline ("D3D12 default on Windows", 4.6 row) and the breaking-changes 4.5 to 4.6 section, versus ADR-0008 l.31 and l.43 (OQ-C).
- **Reality (P-D):** `ProjectSettings.get_setting("rendering/rendering_device/driver.windows")` returned `vulkan` on 4.7.2. ADR-0008 also saw `driver = vulkan` at runtime. The reference text is likely misleading: D3D12 may be the editor or template default only in some distributions. Treat as a doc defect in `docs/engine-reference`, not an ADR defect. ADR-0008 does the right thing by pinning and asserting the effective value.
- **Confidence:** HIGH that the built-in default setting is `vulkan`. MED that nothing else (for example a first-run editor project template) sets D3D12.

The review verdict is **FAIL**, but it comes from one strict rule. The Core-layer ADRs (0011–0019 and 0034) aren't written yet, which leaves 200 Core requirements uncovered, and the skill fails any review with uncovered Foundation or Core requirements. All ten Foundation ADRs are now written, and the only cross-ADR conflicts are medium or low. Without that rule the verdict would be CONCERNS. Nothing is committed.

**Coverage** (1138 requirements, all ADRs still Proposed):

| | This run | Previous run |
|---|---|---|
| Covered by a Proposed ADR | 181 | 50 |
| Partial | 187 | 48 |
| Gap | 770 | 1038 |

- **89** of the gaps are requirements a written Foundation ADR was expected to settle but doesn't.
- **675** belong to ADRs that aren't written yet (0011–0034); they weren't graded against the written ADRs.
- Most partial grades are the same pattern: the Foundation ADR provides the mechanism and leaves system-specific values to the later module ADR.

**What needs fixing before the ADRs can be accepted:**
1. **ADR-0003 has a parse error on 4.7.2 (E1).** `PresentationViews.get(block_id)` overrides the built-in `Object.get()`, and the specialist's probe showed the script fails to load. ADR-0009 uses the same name, and ADR-0010's own naming rule bans it. Rename it to `get_view` or `lookup`.
2. **ADR-0006 cites a "quit transition" in ADR-0001 that doesn't exist.** It should point at ADR-0002/ADR-0003 instead, or ADR-0001 needs a short shutdown paragraph.
3. **ADR-0010 contradicts itself on the sorted-key helper.** §5.3 names `canonical_encoder.gd` and `sorted_string_keys`, but its lint rows still say `sorted_keys.gd` and `sorted_text_keys`. Nine other low-severity wording issues from the last run are also still open.
4. **The dependency script reports 4 cycles.** They aren't a real deadlock: each runs through an edge its own ADR labels "soft". The script can't tell soft from hard, so those references need to move out of the Depends On tables. The safe acceptance order is in the report.
5. **31 requirements contradict their ADR.** In each case the ADR deliberately changed the design and the GDD hasn't caught up. Examples: `restore()` now reports failure through a context instead of returning `(ok, reason, detail)`, and the kernel now does the hashing instead of each block owner. The GDD has to be synced, or the ADR revised, before that ADR is accepted.
6. **96 of the 132 queued sync edits are still unapplied.** That includes 19 in `architecture.md`.

I left the systems index unchanged. The one high-severity engine finding is in ADR text only, and none of the contradicting ADRs is Accepted yet, so marking Approved GDDs as Needs Revision would misstate their status.

content.content:
The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).

`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get(block_id: StringName) -> Object`, returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade (superseded for `PERCEPTION_OUT` by the two-face rule below). **Two faces of `PresentationViews`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07 item 10 and TD-08; ADR-0004 § 2 check 6, ADR-0009 § 1)*: `PresentationViews` carries a `perception_access: bool` that the composition root sets **once, at issue**, and presentation code cannot change. The **default face** (`perception_access == false`, every facet except the two below) answers `get(block_id)` for a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation, exactly as `SimViews` does. The **perception face** (`perception_access == true`) returns the real facade. ADR-0009 § 1 fixes which facets carry the flag: the Perception Filter's `PresentationFacet` and the `DIAGNOSTIC` facets only. The same flag gates the subscription: ADR-0004 § 2 check 6 refuses, at subscribe time and in the kernel, a subscription to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` unless the issuing facet carries `perception_access = true`. A `SIM`-class block is readable through either face. ADR-0024 owns only the Filter's query surface, not this rule.

A fault in `read_view` or `empty_view` at the freeze is recorded and leaves the empty view in place; it never faults the kernel (CR-19(a)). Under `STRICT_DEBUG` the `SIM_WRITE_TRIPWIRE` hashes SIM blocks per dispatch batch and around P5 (`TRIPWIRE_BUDGET_MS` 1.0 ms, full sweep every `TRIPWIRE_SWEEP_TICKS` 60), which catches a facade that leaks a mutable reference.

lines: The kernel never hands out a live container. **Each owner's `read_view(ctx)` is called once, at the registry freeze**, and delivers a long-lived getter-only facade over its block object (typed scalar getters and caller-owned-buffer queries, so hot paths allocate nothing). Each owner also supplies **`empty_view(ctx)`**: a facade of the same class whose getters return neutral values (zero, false, empty) and whose `is_empty()` is true. This replaces the GDD's per-request `read_view` (§ GDD sync); it is valid only because `restore` copies into the existing block object (§ 2).

-`ReadViews` has two faces, issued as facets by the composition root (ADR-0001): **`SimViews`** (to `validate`, `apply` and hooks) and **`PresentationViews`** (to subscribers). Both have `get(block_id: StringName) -> Object`, returning the owner's facade, which the caller casts to the owner's view class. For a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, `SimViews.get` returns that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation; `PresentationViews` returns the real facade (superseded for `PERCEPTION_OUT` by the two-face rule below). **Two faces of `PresentationViews`** *(Amended 2026-10-28, TD-07 item 10 and TD-08; ADR-0004 § 2 check 6, ADR-0009 § 1)*: `PresentationViews` carries a `perception_access: bool` that the composition root sets **once, at issue**, and presentation code cannot change. The **default face** (`perception_access == false`, every facet except the two below) answers `get(block_id)` for a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with that block's typed `empty_view`, increments `PERCEPTION_READ_BLOCKED` and reports a violation, exactly as `SimViews` does. The **perception face** (`perception_access == true`) returns the real facade. ADR-0009 § 1 fixes which facets carry the flag: the Perception Filter's `PresentationFacet` and the `DIAGNOSTIC` facets only. The same flag gates the subscription: ADR-0004 § 2 check 6 refuses, at subscribe time and in the kernel, a subscription to a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block with `SUBSCRIBE_REFUSED` unless the issuing facet carries `perception_access = true`. A `SIM`-class block is readable through either face. ADR-0024 owns only the Filter's query surface, not this rule.

- **Reaping and lifetime.** Each poll calls `wait_to_finish()` **only** on a job whose thread reports `not is_alive()` (probed: returns at once with the callable's value). A dead thread with no terminal `WRITTEN`/`FAILED` status is `SL_WRITE_WORKER_DIED`: `save_status` `FAILED`, `fail_n` + 1, the ring position released, the `.tmp` left to T-6. **A live thread is never joined**: `Thread.wait_to_finish` and the pool wait take no timeout (training knowledge), so a join at the `DEAD` boundary could hang the frame on a hung write. **Every `WriteJob` stays referenced from `SaveService.jobs` until it is reaped or the process exits**, including an abandoned job: a `Thread` object freed while its thread still runs logs the same `~Thread` warning as the quit probe and detaches the worker from any owner, orphaning its buffers, so dropping a live job on abandonment or on `SaveService` teardown is forbidden and a freed live job is a fault in debug builds.

A job that lands a generation after being abandoned is moved to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH`.

Save & Quit therefore **polls** the `QUIT` job under `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` 3 000 on the injected `Clock` and calls `request_shutdown` on `WRITTEN`; on timeout it does not abandon (a late completion is simply a `QUIT` generation, SL-6), reports `FAILED`, and the Chart Table offers the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving". An abandoned worker still running at exit is left to the operating system and its `.tmp` handled by T-6 on the next open. A worker blocked in a syscall rather than a sleep, or one that touches freed singletons while the engine tears down at exit, is **UNVERIFIED** (SAVE-WRK-1 d tests a worker mid-`store_buffer` and mid-`rename` at quit, on dev and release builds; the `quit_requested` check between stages shortens the tail).

**1.7 Single-instance lock (corrects SL-10), Windows-only best effort.** The GDD's `campaign.lock` "created with an exclusive open" is **not implementable with `FileAccess`**: a second WRITE-open of the same path succeeds (probed; WRITE mode truncates per the documented flag semantics). What does work on Windows (probed): a file held open makes `rename_absolute` and `remove_absolute` of it fail with `ERR_FAILED`, for READ and WRITE handles alike. The lock is therefore: the process that opens a campaign keeps a `FileAccess` handle on `campaign.lock` open (write mode, containing its process id, diagnostic only) for the campaign's lifetime; a second process tests ownership by renaming the file to `campaign.lock.probe` and back; a failure means "held", and it opens the campaign **READ_ONLY** (SL-10, AC-SL-147). `DirAccess` reports a missing source and a held target with the same `ERR_FAILED` (probed), so the probe **runs only when `campaign.lock` exists**; a missing file means "not held": the process creates it and holds the handle. A READ handle held for the campaign's lifetime suffices (probed: READ-held targets also fail rename and remove), which avoids depending on WRITE-mode truncation. A crashed holder releases its handle with the process, so there is no stale-lock case and no process-id liveness check is needed (`OS.is_process_running` is probed true for the own id, but whether it answers for a foreign non-child process is **UNVERIFIED** and is not used). **Handle lifetime:** a GDScript `FileAccess` closes when its last reference goes away (scope exit, reassignment, `null`, freeing the owner), so the handle is a **member of `SaveService`** (never a local), is never reassigned or nulled until the campaign closes, and a debug assertion checks `FileAccess.is_open()` in each frame poll. **Accepted exposure:** when the lock is not held the probe moves the file aside for an instant, and a third process starting at that moment sees "missing = not held" and also acquires it; for a single-instance guard this is acceptable and recorded, not engineered around. On Linux and the Deck, rename of an open file is expected to succeed (**UNVERIFIED**, SAVE-WRK-1 g), so the lock gives no protection there; Steam launches a single instance by default. content.text:
I fixed the four ADR issues I offered. The dependency script now reports no cycles, and nothing is committed.

1. **The parse error (E1):** the read-view accessor is now `get_view(block_id)` on both `SimViews` and `PresentationViews`. That covers ADR-0003 (five places), ADR-0009 and the stance in `docs/registry/architecture.yaml`. The name follows ADR-0010's `get_<noun>` rule.
2. **ADR-0010's sorted-key helper:** its lint rows, its `src/shared/` contents row and OQ-N(2) now all name `CanonicalEncoder.sorted_int_keys` / `sorted_string_keys` in `canonical_encoder.gd`. No `sorted_keys.gd` or `sorted_text_keys` mentions remain.
3. **ADR-0006's quit transition:** it now points to ADR-0003's `SHUTTING_DOWN` state, entered only through ADR-0002's `request_shutdown`. It no longer cites ADR-0001.
4. **Dependency cycles:** the soft references now sit in their own rows. ADR-0010 is under "Soft references" in ADR-0004 and ADR-0005, and ADR-0005 is under "Validation follow-up" in ADR-0007. The script's order is now 0001 → 0002 → 0003 → 0004 → 0007 → 0005 → 0010 → 0006 → 0009 → 0008, which matches the hard order in the report.

One thing to know about fix 4: an earlier cross-ADR ruling (TD-27) had deliberately put ADR-0010 in ADR-0004's Depends On row. I kept the reference and only moved its row. Say if you'd rather undo it and have the dependency script skip "soft" entries instead.

Each edited ADR has a dated amendment note. The review report has a "Post-review fixes" section, and I re-stamped its content hashes for the seven edited ADRs. As a result, the next `/architecture-review` will see these ADRs as unchanged rather than re-checking them. The registry validates.

**Still open:**
- ADR-0010 still says packed arrays are handed to the save worker "by value", but they're shared by reference (E4).
- The `dictionary_variant.json` allow-list, which reconciles ADR-0002's untyped payloads with ADR-0010's lint, still has no contents (E5).
- 10 low-severity wording issues.
- ADR-0008's 14.9 ms frame-budget row doesn't exclude autosave frames.
- The GDD sync: 96 queued edits and 31 conflicting requirements.
- The Core ADRs 0011–0019 and 0034.

11 files are modified: seven ADRs, the architecture registry, the review report, the traceability index and the TR registry. Say "commit and push" when you want them committed.
